tour.overview:
The Amalfi Coast runs for about 50 kilometres along the southern side of the Sorrento peninsula, where the Lattari Mountains drop almost straight into the Tyrrhenian Sea. Villages of pastel houses cling to the cliffs, lemon groves climb in terraces held up by dry-stone walls, and a narrow road cut into the rock in the 19th century links them in a series of hairpin bends. In the Middle Ages, Amalfi was one of Italy's four great maritime republics, trading with Constantinople and the Arab world. The coast has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.

This private day lets you enjoy the coast without driving it yourself or fighting for a seat on the crowded buses. Your driver stops at the best viewpoints, leaves you free time in Positano, guides you to Amalfi's cathedral and cloister and takes you up to Ravello, the quiet garden town above the sea where Wagner found inspiration. Lunch is at a restaurant with a sea view, and the day ends with a taste of limoncello made from the coast's large, fragrant lemons.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Sorrento, Naples or on the Amalfi Coast
• Type: private tour with car and English-speaking driver; local guide in Amalfi and Ravello on request
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; short walks, with steps and steep lanes in Positano and Ravello

WHAT YOU SEE
• Photo stops on the coast road above Positano.
• Positano: the beach, the church of Santa Maria Assunta and the lanes.
• Amalfi: the cathedral of St Andrew, the Cloister of Paradise and the piazza.
• Ravello: Villa Rufolo and its gardens, and the cathedral square.
• A limoncello tasting.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your driver knows where to stop and park on a road where both are very hard, and adapts the direction of the day to the traffic, so you spend your time in the villages, not in queues.

WHO IT SUITS
Couples, families and anyone who wants to see the classic Amalfi Coast comfortably in one day.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer to see the coast from the water, ask us about a private boat day from Positano or Amalfi. If you suffer badly from car sickness, a boat is also the better choice.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The coast road is very narrow and winding: tell us if you are prone to car sickness and we will plan more stops. In July and August traffic is heavy and we start earlier. Cars cannot enter Positano's lower lanes: you walk down and your driver collects you at the top.

days.name: Coast road viewpoints, Positano, Amalfi Cathedral and Cloister of Paradise, lunch by the sea and the gardens of Ravello
days.description:
What to expect: the three most beautiful villages of the Amalfi Coast in one relaxed day, with a private car and driver, tickets, lunch and limoncello.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 8:30. From Sorrento, the road crosses the ridge of the peninsula and comes down on the Amalfi side, where the whole coast opens up in front of you. The first stop is a viewpoint above Positano, the village of pink, yellow and white houses that tumbles down the cliff to the sea – the picture that made the Amalfi Coast famous after John Steinbeck wrote about it in 1953.

Your driver drops you at the top of the village and you walk down through lanes of linen shops and sandal makers to the beach and the church of Santa Maria Assunta, with its dome of majolica tiles. You have about an hour and a half to wander, have a coffee or put your feet in the sea. Your driver collects you on the main road and continues along the cliffs, past the fishing village of Praiano and the deep inlet of the Fjord of Furore, to Amalfi.

In Amalfi, the steps of the Cathedral of St Andrew rise above the main square. The church, founded in the 9th century and rebuilt many times, has a striped façade and a bronze door cast in Constantinople in the 11th century; the relics of the apostle Andrew lie in the crypt. Beside it, the Cloister of Paradise, built around 1266 as a burial place for noble families, has white interlaced arches that show the Arab influence on this trading town. Lunch is at a restaurant overlooking the sea: fresh fish, scialatielli pasta with seafood, or lemon-scented dishes.

In the afternoon you drive up the valley to Ravello, 350 metres above the sea. You visit the gardens of Villa Rufolo, a 13th-century merchant's palace whose terraces inspired Richard Wagner in 1880 and which host a famous summer music festival, with one of the most photographed views on the coast. Before heading back, you taste limoncello made from the large, sweet Sfusato lemons of Amalfi. You are back at your hotel at about 17:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:30 – Viewpoint above Positano.
09:45 – Free time in Positano (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
11:30 – Drive along the coast past Praiano and the Fjord of Furore.
12:15 – Amalfi Cathedral and the Cloister of Paradise.
13:15 – Lunch with sea view in Amalfi.
15:00 – Ravello: Villa Rufolo and the cathedral square.
16:15 – Limoncello tasting and drive back.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Traffic on the coast road can be heavy in summer; your driver may reverse the order of the villages to avoid queues.
• The gardens of Villa Cimbrone, with the Terrace of Infinity, can replace or follow Villa Rufolo.
• A licensed local guide for Amalfi and Ravello can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, tickets to Amalfi Cathedral and the Cloister of Paradise and Villa Rufolo, lunch, limoncello tasting, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: licensed local guide (on request), drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is a guide included?
faq.answer: Your driver speaks English and tells you about the coast along the way. A licensed local guide for Amalfi and Ravello can be added on request; drivers are not allowed to guide inside the monuments.

faq.question: Can we start from Naples or Rome?
faq.answer: From Naples, yes, with about 1 hour 15 minutes more driving each way. From Rome the day is very long; we suggest at least one night in Sorrento or on the coast.

faq.question: I get car sick. Is the road difficult?
faq.answer: The road has many tight bends. Sit in the front, tell your driver, and we will plan more stops. If you suffer badly, a private boat day is a better way to see the coast.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Amalfi Cathedral with the Cloister of Paradise, and Villa Rufolo in Ravello.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a restaurant with a sea view, usually in Amalfi. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Will we have time to swim?
faq.answer: Yes, if you wish. Bring a swimsuit and we can give you more time on the beach in Positano or Amalfi instead of one of the visits.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the beaches, the boats and the gelato. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Positano and Ravello have many steps and steep lanes, and the cathedral of Amalfi is reached by a long staircase. The views from the car are wonderful; tell us your needs and we will adapt the day.

faq.question: Can we add a boat trip?
faq.answer: Yes. A private boat from Positano to Amalfi, past grottoes and beaches, can replace part of the drive. The price depends on the boat and the season.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes for steps, sun protection and a swimsuit if you want to swim. For the cathedral, cover your shoulders and knees.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May, June, September and early October. July and August are beautiful but very busy; from November to March many shops and restaurants close.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
